newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aussie dlr steadies but evidence inconclusive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aussie dlr steadies but evidence inconclusive.

text.p: The Australian dollar loitered in a seven tick range Thursday as caution after its recent retreat and a holiday in Tokyo conspired to kill trade.

Traders said a couple of days of inconclusive action had established US$0.7850 as solid support, but equally US$0.7910 had proved to be resilient resistance. The market was content to let it consolidate while deciding if this week's retreat from 80 cents was a blip or the start of a more protracted retracement.
Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane made a few comments on inflation and the economy but they were so generalised analysts were hard pressed to find a policy message in them.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the dollar had crept to US$0.7875/80 from an early US$0.7870/75 and US$0.7861/66 late here Wednesday.

A break of US$0.7835 would suggest the correction had further to run, with US$0.7550 a favourite target amongst chart watchers, while clearing US$0.7910 would confirm to many that the selloff was temporary and a re-test of 80 cents was on the cards.

On the crosses, the mark came under pressure against the yen and Swiss franc and the dollar edged up to 1.3260/71 marks from 1.3188/04 late Wednesday. It was steady on the yen at 96.71/81 from 96.63/73 and unchanged in trade weighted terms at 60.6.

Macfarlane said for the foreseeable future he expected underlying inflation to remain around the 2.1 percent level seen in the December quarter and the economy was free of major macro-economic imbalances.
The governor also said the government had more to do on the fiscal front, which some analysts took to mean he did not think fiscal policy was especially tight at the moment.

That, they said, could be taken to imply the bank would not feel inclined to ease monetary policy just because the government delivered a tough budget in May, as some market commentators have suggested.
Treasurer Peter Costello was also on the wires saying recent indicators supported the view the economy would continue to strengthen.
He pointed to Wednesday's strong Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index, rising building approvals and corporate profits.

Costello also noted today's skilled vacancies index from the Employment Department which showed the fifth consecutive monthly increase in March. Vacancies rose 2.0 percent after a 0.7 percent rise the month before. There is little in the way of domestic data due for the next week.
